title: LLMs for Generating and Evaluating Counterfactuals: A Comprehensive Study

bias_targets.methodology: Prompting LLMs to act as evaluators on an 'honest set' (where correct ground truth labels are provided) and a 'corrupted set' (where incorrect labels are provided) to measure the models' tendency to blindly agree with the provided labels.

Comparing the evaluation scores GPT-4 assigns to its own generated counterfactuals versus those generated by other LLMs and humans, to determine if the model disproportionately favors its own outputs.

Conducting qualitative analysis on cases where GPT-4 assigned lower scores to human expert generations compared to its own, revealing that the model penalizes texts containing potentially harmful or negative content even when safety is not a requested evaluation criterion.
